update.title: Built a real-time webcam background removal pipeline
update.summary: Built a real-time webcam pipeline that uses Robust Video Matting to separate the foreground, replace or blur the background, and expose the result as a standard V4L2 camera.

preview.description: RVM composited output placing a person against a solid blue virtual background

blocks.body:
## Turn background removal into an ordinary camera

I built RVM Virtual Camera so real-time background removal works in applications that do not need to know about the model behind it. The program opens a physical webcam, passes each frame through a Robust Video Matting model loaded with PyTorch, composites the foreground, and writes the finished frame to a V4L2 loopback device.

OBS, conferencing tools, and browser calls can select that output like an ordinary camera.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  Camera[Physical webcam] --> Capture[Threaded frame capture]
  Capture --> RVM[Robust Video Matting model]
  RVM --> Matte[Foreground and alpha matte]
  Background[Solid color, image, or blurred frame] --> Composite[Frame composition]
  Matte --> Composite
  Composite --> Preview[Optional preview]
  Composite --> V4L2[V4L2 loopback camera]
  V4L2 --> Calls[OBS, browser, or call application]
blocks.description: The machine-learning pipeline terminates at a standard virtual-camera boundary, keeping consumers independent of the model.

blocks.body:
## Keep the frame loop practical

Capture runs on its own thread, keeping camera reads separate from inference and the optional preview. Resolution, frame-rate, downsample, and model controls provide practical ways to balance image quality and throughput against available GPU capacity.

The pipeline can place the subject over a solid color or chosen image, or blur the source background while preserving the foreground. Its preview combines the source frame, composited result, and alpha matte side by side so each stage can be checked before another application consumes the virtual camera.

blocks.body:
## Make the host boundary explicit

Camera input, processed output device, optional raw passthrough device, model, resolution, frame rate, background mode, and downsample ratio are command-line options rather than one workstation's hardcoded settings. The output uses a loaded `v4l2loopback` device, while CUDA and half-precision inference make the model practical at interactive frame rates.
